title: CI is green on Windows and Linux for the 3.2.0 release commit
description: Release blocker for 3.2.0. CI run 37865326884 on release/v3.2.0 (4aaad089) failed selftests on windows-latest in eight files and one browser leg in manifest validation on Linux. Most of the work since 3.1.0 had never run on Windows.
desiredOutcome: the CI workflow passes on every job at the release commit, Windows selftests and the Linux manifest-validation browser legs included

tasks.title: Windows: test__output rt3 holds on Windows
tasks.description: On windows-latest, plugins/audit/tests/test__output.py fails case rt3: 'a tree the plain removal could not take is removed by the fallback pass without changing the mode of a file OUTSIDE it that a link inside it points at: mode 666'.

outcome.technical:
The fault was in rt3's fixture, not in _output.remove_tree. rt3 set the link target to 0o640 and compared the mode afterwards with that literal. On Windows, os.chmod keeps only the read-only attribute, so 0o640 reads back as 0o666 and the check could never pass. A writable target also reads the same before and after a chmod through the link, so on Windows the case could not catch the defect it exists for.

The target is now read-only (stat.S_IREAD) and is compared with its own mode as read back. The owner-write bit is the one permission fact both platforms keep, and remove_tree's fallback chmod (0o700) sets it. A new case, rt3a, asserts the target has no owner-write bit before the removal, so a return to a writable fixture goes red instead of leaving rt3 unable to fail. rt3's message now prints both modes.

Only the test file changed.

The red was observed by simulation, not on Windows: scratchpad P121.1/probe.py emulates Windows chmod.
- HEAD's rt3 is red with the real remove_tree, matching CI's "mode 666".
- The fixed file is green.
- A link-following remove_tree mutant is red with the fixed file, on POSIX and on emulated Windows.

The helper could not run: macOS has no red to observe.
outcome.descriptive: A test that checks safe folder removal now works on Windows, where file permissions are reduced to read-only or writable.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: Windows chmod emulation shows HEAD red and the fix green; a link-following mutant stays red on both platforms

tasks.title: Windows: test_audit_task finishes well inside the sweep cap
tasks.description: On windows-latest, plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py did not finish within the sweep's 300-second per-file cap. Profile it first. Then run its stages concurrently in child processes and replay their results, the way tests/test_drive_phase.py has done since P119.7. Every case id and verdict must stay identical; diff the case lists before and after. Do not raise the cap.

outcome.technical:
Profile first: at-block (786 cases, 93.9 s) dominated, and the time goes to process starts, about 7,200 per full run. The full HEAD run took 222 s on a loaded machine.

at-block is split into seven slices (at1-block to at7-block), cut only at group boundaries where an AST data-flow check showed no later group reads a name an earlier group bound. Shared opening helpers moved unchanged to `_at_kit(tmp)`. Imports were hoisted to module level, which removed five local-before-assignment reads.

The full run now starts every stage as a child (`--stage X --cases-to f.json`), at most six at once, with a 280 s timeout per child. It replays the cases in STAGES order through one `_harness.run` and runs label_faults over the merged call sites. A child that reports nothing is one named failure. `--stage` without `--cases-to` still runs in process, so the red helper's narrowed runs are unchanged.

New ps-block:
- ps1: every `_at_kit` caller is in STAGES.
- ps1b: a missing slice is named.
- ps2: a silent block is one named failure.
- ps3: a replayed stage matches the same stage run in process.

All 894 original case ids and verdicts are identical and in the same order.

Two runs, about 25 minutes apart: 28.5 s and 28.0 s, against 222 s before.

Windows simulation (scratchpad P121.2/probe, a delay added to every process start): HEAD hit the 300 s cap, and the fixed copy finished in 141 s.

Each of four mutations turned its own case red.

The runner helpers are copies of test_drive_phase.py's. Moving them into tests/_harness.py is the better structure and is recorded internally.
outcome.descriptive: The largest test file now runs its parts in parallel, about eight times faster, with exactly the same tests and results, so the Windows run stays inside its time limit.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: profile-led split; identical case ids and verdicts; slow-spawn Windows simulation HEAD timed out, fix 141 s

tasks.title: Windows: concurrent usage appends lose no row
tasks.description: On windows-latest, plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_usage.py fails case bw3: 'appenders for sessions outside the backfill set, running during a backfill, lose no row across repeated trials: appended 932, lost 97'. This may be a real data-loss bug on Windows, not a flaky test: a rename over an open file, or an append racing a rewrite without a lock. Find out which, and if it is real, fix the code.

outcome.technical:
This was real data loss on Windows, not a flaky test. Windows refuses os.replace onto a file any handle holds open, so the backfill's month rewrite was refused on its first try. HEAD's retry then drained, closed, and wrote the whole month to a temp file before the swap, and any row an appender wrote in that window was erased. A retry refused again failed the month.

Fix, in usage_ledger.py: a per-month OS lock (fcntl.flock on POSIX, msvcrt.locking on Windows) on `<month>.jsonl.lock`, which is never deleted and is not selected by any `.jsonl` reader.
- append_rows opens, writes and closes under the lock. If the lock is not free within MONTH_LOCK_WAIT_S, it appends anyway: a row at risk rather than a row dropped for certain.
- rewrite_month holds the lock for the last drain, the temp write and the replace. It retries a refused replace under the lock, then settles for writers that take no lock. If it cannot get the lock, it returns False and leaves the old file standing.
- New functions: month_lock_path, lock_month, unlock_month, _append_locked and _replace_retrying. _write_rows is removed.
- audit-usage.py's docstring and comment are updated.

Decision, reversing an earlier design pin: case bw7 ("append_rows still takes no lock", named in the done task P107.3's verifiedBy) is removed, because a lock-free append cannot be made safe on Windows. `tools/bench-hooks.py --gate` passes. tw4 expects the lock file. nm1's writer appends directly, so it still tests writers that take no lock.

New cases:
- bw14 reproduces the Windows sequence deterministically.
- bw15 and lk1-lk3 cover the lock itself.

Red-first: proved (bw14 red at HEAD).

Mutations, in a copied tree, each red on its cases:
- no lock on append;
- append gives up when the lock is busy;
- append never unlocks;
- rewrite takes no lock;
- rewrite never unlocks.

The Windows-replace probe (scratchpad P121.3/probe_windows_replace.py) lost 24, 52, 46, 19 and 11 rows over five trials on a HEAD export, and none on the working tree.

Not run on Windows. The build guide still says the metering hook appends without a lock; that line is carried by the next task in this phase.
outcome.descriptive: Cost records written while the monthly ledger is being rewritten are no longer lost on Windows; appends and the rewrite share a per-month lock.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: real data loss reproduced by a Windows-replace probe on HEAD, none after; bw14 proved red; lock mutations each red

tasks.title: Windows: close-phase's symlink case holds on Windows
tasks.description: On windows-latest, plugins/audit/tests/test_close_phase.py fails case cr28: 'a declared symbolic link to a file that did not change lands BOUND'. It printed exit 1 and landed False, with 'REFUSED: does not land over its newest gate verdict'.

outcome.technical:
Cause: before landing, close-phase checks the branch tip out into a scratch work tree and fingerprints the declared files against the gate's recorded fingerprint. The recorder reads a symlink through to its target's bytes. `_check_out` decided whether a file was a link by asking the checked-out file. Under core.symlinks=false, git's Windows default, checkout-index writes a link as a plain file holding the target's path text, so the tip's fingerprint hashed that text and the phase was refused as moved (cr28 on windows-latest).

Fix: a link is identified by its mode in the tip's tree and read from git, not from the filesystem.
- `_link_texts()` takes the mode-120000 entries from `git ls-files -s -z` and reads each link's target with `git cat-file blob`.
- `_check_out` returns `(work_tree, links)`.
- `_leads_to()` follows a chain of links to the file whose bytes reading the link yields.
- `_write_tip` reads that file.
- A cycle of links leaves the check unestablished, so the phase is refused as unanswerable, because the recorder cannot read a cycle either.

Cases, reproduced on macOS by setting `core.symlinks false` in the fixture repo:
- cr30: an unchanged link target lands bound;
- cr31: a target changed after the green still refuses as moved (the second direction);
- the skip list for hosts that refuse os.symlink covers cr28-cr31.

Red-first: proved (cr30 red at HEAD, 246/247).

Probe (scratchpad P121.4/probe.py): HEAD MISMATCH, working tree MATCH.

Observed, recorded internally: cr22 counts close-phase-tip-* directories in the shared system TMPDIR, so it can flake when the suite runs outside the sweep beside another process.
outcome.descriptive: Merging a phase that contains a symbolic link no longer fails on Windows, where git writes links as plain files.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: link identified by tree mode and read from git; core.symlinks=false reproduces the Windows refusal; cr30 proved red, cr31 second direction

tasks.title: Windows: drive-phase prints and sign-off hold on Windows
tasks.description: On windows-latest, plugins/audit/tests/test_drive_phase.py fails three cases: dp3, where a success print of 400 bytes exceeds the 300-byte bound, likely because of Windows paths; and sg2 and gr1, the sign-off and commit sequences.

outcome.technical:
Root cause of dp3, sg2 and gr1 on Windows: the journal was appended in text mode, so Windows wrote CRLF into the committed blob. close-phase's pending_beyond_stamp read the working journal in text mode, which folded CRLF to LF, and compared it with `git show HEAD:`, which keeps CRLF. _foreign_rows then concluded the journal no longer began with HEAD's, and the landing stamp was skipped. That left sg2 and gr1 dirty, and grew dp3's final print to 400 bytes. A sitecustomize that gives text-mode writes the Windows newline reproduced all three on macOS, with CI's exact sizes.

(b) Every trail and ledger append now writes LF on every platform:
- _journal_io's appender and write_merged;
- _evidence_io.append_row;
- usage_ledger._append_locked;
- hooks/_config's append_gate_event and atomic_write_text.

The hash chain hashes each row's canonical JSON before it is written, so line endings never enter it. Readers split lines and accept CRLF, so old CRLF rows still verify. nl6 checks this end to end on a real repo.

(a) close-phase reads the journal with newline="" and folds CRLF to LF on both sides before the prefix check. A core.autocrlf checkout (CRLF over an LF blob) therefore still lands; cl3 pins that.

Cases:
- nl0: the simulation really writes CRLF.
- nl1-nl5: each writer writes LF under it.
- nl6: an old CRLF trail still verifies.
- cl1: a CRLF-committed journal lands.
- cl2: the over-fire twin, where another phase's row is still named.
- cl3: an autocrlf checkout lands.

Red-first: proved for close-phase (cl1, cl2). For the journal, the helper's fix run missed _evidence_io.py, which was declared at a wrong path, now corrected. Scratch mutations turned nl1-nl5, cl3 and cl2 red.

Under the Windows-newline simulation the driver suite passes 128/128, and the full sweep passes 316/316. `tools/bench-hooks.py --gate` passes, because hooks import _config.

The build guide's audit-usage section now describes the per-month lock and the line endings.

Same class, left and recorded internally: _manifest_io.atomic_write_text and the demo generators' committed .jsonl writers.
outcome.descriptive: The audit trail and ledgers are written the same way on every platform, and merging a phase on Windows now commits its final record instead of leaving it behind.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: root cause reproduced by a Windows-newline simulation with CI's exact values; fix green under it; cl1/cl2 proved red; mutations red

tasks.title: Windows: measure-context counts the same bytes on Windows
tasks.description: On windows-latest, `tools/measure-context.py --selftest` fails case mc3 ('the entry's total is its body plus those files, to the byte') and case mc4 ('an agent loads its system prompt and every skill its frontmatter preloads'). The likely cause is CRLF line endings or path separators.

outcome.technical:
Root cause: the selftest's fixture writer _fx_write opened files in text mode. On Windows that writes every `\n` as `\r\n`, but the writer returned the length of the LF text, while the tool reads files in binary. Every fixture size came out short by one byte per newline, which turned mc3 and mc4 red; mc15, mc16, mc20 and mc22 share the same writer.

What changed in tools/measure-context.py:
- _fx_write opens with newline="", so the bytes on disk are the bytes it counts.
- split_frontmatter now charges the closing delimiter's line ending, `\r\n` or `\n`, to the frontmatter rather than to the body. Before, a CRLF checkout's body started with a stray `\r\n`.
- The tool still measures the bytes actually on disk, and does not normalise CRLF.

New cases:
- mc28: a fixture file's size on disk equals the size of the text it was given.
- mc29: CRLF and LF frontmatter split the same way, and a blank line that opens the body still counts.

Windows behaviour was simulated with a text-mode write that turns `\n` into `\r\n` (scratchpad P121.8/probe.py --windows), on scratch copies:
- HEAD: 21/27, with mc3, mc4, mc15, mc16, mc20 and mc22 red.
- Fixed: 29/29, plain and simulated.
- Mutants: restoring the text-mode write turns mc28 red; restoring the LF-only split, or stripping every leading newline, turns mc29 red.

Red-first: the helper refused, because the task declares no test file (the cases are inline in tools/).
outcome.descriptive: The context-size tool counts the same bytes on Windows, where text files get CRLF line endings.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: CRLF-write simulation turns HEAD red and the fix green; mc28 and mc29 each red under their mutant

tasks.title: Linux: the hostile-row leg holds on this repo's plan in CI
tasks.description: In ubuntu CI, the 'The report is interactive' step of the manifest-validation job fails on the live-plan render of docs/audit/audit-plan.json: 'a very long summary and a very long unbroken token, planted in phases + data bugs, widen the document at no width: got 833px (826 -> 873)'. The same check passes on macOS. Render the plan and find the cell in the bugs data table that widens under Linux fonts; the reviewer's probes are in scratchpad/probe/. Fix the cause, or the check's assumption, without weakening what the check guards.

outcome.technical:
Cause: section 10b planted the long summary into every bare cell of the bugs table, including status, severity and ADO, whose real values are a pill, a single word or a dash. At 833px, the first width above the 52rem breakpoint, the eight-column bugs table is already at its minimum width with real content. One ordinary planted word widened those columns under Linux's wider fonts. A Verdana stand-in reproduced CI's shape: 833 -> 877, against CI's 826 -> 873.

Decision: fix the check's assumption, not the CSS. The renderer never puts a paragraph in a status, severity or count column. A cell is planted if it is full-width, or if it is a bare-text cell in a column where the rendered plan itself holds words separated by spaces. The token, the chips and the widening assertion are unchanged. Tables with no prose cell are named as skipped in the notes. The cost in coverage: two data tables per shipped report that hold only numbers or single words are no longer planted.

Probe (scratchpad P121.9/measure.mjs; old or new planting, mac or wide font):
- live plan and demo-large: old+wide red, new+wide green;
- acme and index: green in all four combinations;
- with the new planting, colspan cells not breaking turns it red, and data cells set nowrap turns it red.

Separate, and already recorded internally: the live bugs table has no width to spare at 833px on Linux, so a real title word longer than the current widest would widen the page.
outcome.descriptive: The report check stops failing on Linux fonts over an ordinary word placed in a status column, and still fails when long text can widen the page.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: wide-font stand-in turns the old planting red and the new green; two CSS breakages still red

tasks.title: Windows: shipped text files check out with LF everywhere
tasks.description: On windows-latest the CRLF checkout inflates every shipped .md file: tools/measure-context.py mc19/mc24 measure the reviewer at 7126 against its 7000 ceiling and /audit:phase at 4028 against 4000 (6995 and 3962 on LF), and test_audit_task.py fb15 fails on the same gate. .gitattributes already pins ui assets, _ui_theme.py, *.sh and *.yml to LF, each with its reason. Extend the pin, with its reason, to every text file the plugin ships or the pipeline commits byte-for-byte: at least *.md, *.json and *.jsonl (the committed journal, evidence and manifest), and decide whether a repo-wide `* text=auto eol=lf` is the cleaner rule. Confirm `git add --renormalize .` changes no indexed content, and that a scratch clone made with core.autocrlf=true now checks these files out LF and measure-context --gate passes there. Add a lint or case so a newly shipped text type that is not pinned is caught, if the repo has a natural home for it (test__refs or measure-context). This is CI round 2 on windows-latest; the job log was saved outside the repository for the executor (grep the file name). You cannot run Windows here. Find the root cause, reproduce the Windows condition locally where you can (a CRLF checkout via `git -c core.autocrlf=true` into a scratch clone, no symlink privilege, a slow process start), show it red before the fix and green after, and say plainly what could not be simulated. Fix the class, not only the named case; a platform skip only with the house's idiom and a stated reason.
